The same conventions, commands, and boundaries have to be repeated over and over—and later conversations can still make the same mistakes as the first one. This pattern is straightforward: drop a project-level config file that loads automatically each session. It spells out build commands, test procedures, architecture rules, naming conventions, and similar content. The file lives with the codebase rather than relying on someone copy-pasting it each time. **Use cases**: repeatedly working on the same codebase across multiple sessions. **Trade-offs**: there is a maintenance cost. The file must stay in sync with the project; once it goes stale, it misleads the agent—worse than not having one.
